A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same variational noise-coupling work. All pages, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation FID results, coupling ablations, gradient-variance measurements and toy experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds gradient-clipping controls and 100k-iteration ImageNet results.

M1.justification: The encoder, Gaussian coupling, consistency-plus-KL objective and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. Section 6.2 restores beta in the expanded KL-weight formula, making it consistent with the already stated definition; this does not establish a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, FFHQ 64×64, class-conditional ImageNet 64×64 and the two-dimensional Gaussian-mixture toy task. Added experiments vary training conditions within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 9–10 substantially broaden quantitative comparisons beyond the retained iCT/ECM and OT controls. They tabulate cited results for additional comparators including iCT-deep, CTM, TCM, sCT, PFGM++, LSGM and several distillation methods; these are not established as new reimplementations.

E3.justification: V2 adds baseline evaluations with and without gradient clipping and 100k-iteration ImageNet runs at batch size 128. The latter use beta=100 for ECM-LI-VC after beta=90 diverged. These supplement the retained main protocols, including the existing 200k-iteration ImageNet experiments.

E4.justification: Appendices C.4–C.5 add substantive checks of two important questions: whether clipping explains the coupling gains, and whether those gains persist with shorter ImageNet training. Tables 6–8 provide new controls and convergence evidence beyond the retained beta ablation, gradient-variance analysis and toy demonstrations.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 retains training seed 42 and sampling/FID seed 32. Neither version reports repeated-run FID uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests; the existing gradient-variance visualization is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their values, while Tables 6–10 add substantial results. For example, the new 100k ImageNet comparison reports ECM-LI-VC FID 6.34/3.77 versus ECM-LI 5.63/3.48 for one/two steps. These are additional settings, not changed 200k results. Table 7's apparent ECM-LI-VC entry reports 2.39, conflicting with 3.39 in Tables 3 and 9, and has an inconsistent method label.

T1.justification: Equation 8 gains an N factor, and Section 6.1 introduces Proposition 6.1. Appendix B substantially replaces the earlier derivation with corrected likelihood signs, triangle and Cauchy–Schwarz inequalities, explicit partition assumptions, and a Taylor/Riemann-sum argument connecting the discrete bound to a continuous-time objective.

C1.justification: The central contribution and headline performance claims remain: learned variational coupling improves CT, achieves leading CIFAR-10 performance and comparable two-step ImageNet performance. The VCT name and revised abstract emphasize capabilities already described in v1; the conclusion is unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C.4 attributes the main gains to coupling rather than clipping. Appendix C.5 adds specific limitations: short ImageNet runs can diverge with small beta and can match or trail baselines, which the authors attribute to insufficient encoder training. V1 already discussed the need for longer convergence, but lacked these specific qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly documents coarse and refined beta searches and reuse of selected values across kernels and datasets. C.5 documents the short-run beta adjustment. Existing architecture, hardware, training-time tables and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds diffusion-coupling references by Bartosh and colleagues and Nielsen and colleagues, while Appendix D adds literature supporting the broader comparisons. The central positioning as a coupling improvement complementary to existing CT methods remains unchanged. Several other reference changes are publication or title updates.

P1.justification: V2 adds the VCT title prefix, rewrites the abstract and part of the introduction, and adds acknowledgments and an impact statement. Appendix C gains subsections and the new comparison appendix shifts former Appendices D–F to E–G; most existing prose and the main narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: Five new tables provide paired clipping comparisons, shorter-training results and extensive comparisons grouped by model family, sampling steps and parameter count. Existing Table 3 changes from full-width to single-column presentation, and Figures 2–3 are repositioned. The original figures and sample images are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves auditability through important algebraic corrections, explicit beta-selection details, clipping controls and disclosure of unfavorable short-budget results. These strengthen the support and qualifications missing from v1. However, new method-label errors and the conflicting FID in Table 7 weaken part of the added evidence, limiting the overall gain.
